transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-21
Time: 11:00am PT / 2:00pm ET
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jason Park (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Millbrook - Head of ML), Marcus Hale (Millbrook - CTO), Priya Kapoor (Millbrook - Infra Lead)

Summary: Quick renewal and expansion check-in. Customer currently on hosted Redwood plan with 2 dedicated pools for core inference. Discussed capacity upgrades (reserve more GPUs), adding eu-west region, contract extension pricing, and security/compliance gating for private VPC. Agreed next steps: send renewal pricing, benchmark data, confirm regions.

Topics:
- Current utilization and pain points
- Options for Dedicated/reserved capacity and burst
- Multi-region expansion (eu-west-1)
- Contract term and pricing (monthly vs annual commit)
- Security/compliance: SSO, SOC2, KMS, audit logs

Action items (captured quickly): Jason to send proposal; Maya to share bench spreadsheet; Marcus to confirm regions.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jason Park: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, we'll keep this tight, we've got about 45 minutes. Maya and I are here from Redwood. Lena, Marcus, Priya, you all good on time?
[00:12] Marcus Hale: Yep, all set. Thanks Jason.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: Yup, good to go.
[00:18] Maya Singh: Cool. Quick agenda - renewal timeline, capacity needs, region add, security Qs, and then we'll recap next steps. Sound ok?
[00:27] Marcus Hale: Sounds perfect. We're basically coming up on our contract renewal in mid-August, want to lock in whatever we can before end of July if possible.
[00:36] Jason Park: Great, that gives us a couple weeks. Quick check - today you run with the hosted plan, two dedicated pools for prod and staging, is that still accurate?
[00:46] Priya Kapoor: Yeah that's right. Prod pool is 8 A100-equivalents-ish, staging is 2. We're seeing peak latency spikes during nightly batch runs and some queueing.
[00:58] Lena Ortiz: Also the model footprint increased - KV cache size is bigger now, so memory pressure is higher. Sorry, I always call it KV cash in notes, ha.
[01:07] Maya Singh: (laughs) totally, KV cash is a classic. Ok, so two visible asks - more baseline capacity for peak, and add eu-west region because we have EU customers and data residency requirements.
[01:20] Marcus Hale: Exactly. We also want to discuss pricing for committing to more capacity and possibly a 12 month extension vs a month-to-month bump.
[01:29] Jason Park: Understood. Quick numbers from our side - based on your telemetry we've seen average 75% utilization across prod pool with 3x occasional spikes, so recommended path is reserved + burst. We can present a tiered commit (e.g., add 4 reserved GPUs to reach steady headroom plus 8 burstable GPUs enabled for nightly jobs). Does that map to what you're thinking?
[01:55] Priya Kapoor: That maps. For EU region, we need dedicated capacity in eu-west-1 or similar with private networking back to our VPC. Are private deployments available there?
[02:08] Maya Singh: Yes, we can do Private deployments in eu-west-1. There's two approaches: 1) Dedicated hosted capacity provisioned in that region with VPC peering and KMS integration, or 2) Private on-prem/VPC package. Since you asked for data residency but still want managed control, likely the Dedicated + VPC peering option works.
[02:27] Marcus Hale: Can you confirm KMS/HSM options? We need envelope encryption with our key material or HSM-backed keys.
[02:36] Jason Park: Absolutely. We support cloud KMS integrations and HSM-based key management for Private customers. We'll include the security appendix showing SOC2 scope and key management options.
[02:46] Lena Ortiz: Great. Also on perf - we ran a quick test last week that showed token latency rising 20% when sequence length goes to 2k. Curious if there are kernel/quantization recs.
[02:59] Maya Singh: Yeah we saw those patterns in your logs. For longer sequences we recommend 8-bit quant plus our tuned kernel selection - sometimes our system will auto-select a different kernel path; that combined with prefix KV caching helps. We'll send the detailed bench that shows cost/latency tradeoffs. Expect to see about 15-25% cost savings with minimal latency hit for your workload in our tests.
[03:22] Marcus Hale: When you say 8-bit quant, are you concerned about any regression on quality? Our QA team will need sample diffs.
[03:30] Maya Singh: Good call. For sensitive generation we recommend running an eval set - we can run a small QA evaluation and provide metrics like BLEU/ROUGE or task-specific accuracy on your test set. We can include that in the PoC.
[03:41] Jason Park: On pricing, we usually provide a renewal with options: monthly committed units or an annual commit with a discount. I'll draft three tiers aligned to the reserved+burst idea.
[03:51] Priya Kapoor: One gating item - our security group needs SSO via SAML matched to Okta and RBAC scoped to teams. How mature is Redwood's SSO?
[04:01] Maya Singh: We support SAML/Okta SSO and SCIM provisioning. RBAC roles are configurable and we also expose audit logs for every inference request and config change. We'll attach our SAML setup guide and audit log retention policies.
[04:14] Marcus Hale: Perfect. For compliance we need evidence of SOC2 and penetration test schedule - do you have latest reports?
[04:21] Jason Park: Yes, SOC2 Type II report is available under NDA; I can send the redacted copy. We also publish summary of our pentest cadence.
[04:30] Lena Ortiz: Moving back to capacity - if we add eu-west region with dedicated capacity, is cross-region fall back automatic? We want traffic to failover to us-east in case of region outage.
[04:42] Maya Singh: Smart routing can be configured so that production puts eu-west first for EU users, fallback to us-east if capacity or region fails. We can set policies by latency, cost, or region. There is also an automatic fallback toggle in console.
[04:56] Marcus Hale: Ok good. One more question on metrics - can you provide token-level cost breakdowns per route so we can attribute spend to product teams?
[05:05] Jason Park: Yes, Redwood Console has token-level cost dashboards per model/route and we can provide API access to export that data.
[05:13] Priya Kapoor: On the network side we need to ensure private networking - can the peering be done with our Transit Gateway? We use AWS TGW heavily.
[05:21] Maya Singh: Yes, we do TGW peering patterns. We'll share the network runbook for TGW and VPC peering, including IP ranges, RPs, and expected maintenance windows.
[05:31] Marcus Hale: About the renewal timing - if we sign an annual commit we want to coordinate a mid-term capacity review at 6 months to adjust quant/cluster sizing. Is that supported?
[05:41] Jason Park: Absolutely. We schedule quarterly business reviews and can do a 6-month capacity tune. We can codify that in the SLA addendum.
[05:49] Lena Ortiz: Great. Anything on the legal side? We have procurement questions about termination and data deletion timelines.
[05:57] Jason Park: We'll include standard termination clauses and a data retention/deletion appendix with timelines for deletion and certificate of deletion. For enterprise deals we also add a 30-60 day transition support.
[06:08] Marcus Hale: Ok. You mentioned benchmarks - can you give a summary now of expected latency improvements if we move to reserved + tuned quant?
[06:16] Maya Singh: From our internal tests on similar workloads, reserved capacity with tuned kernels and prefix caching reduced p95 by ~20-30% and cost per token by ~15-25% depending on model and sequence length. We'll share your customer-specific bench numbers in the sheet.
[06:30] (brief cross talk)
[06:32] Priya Kapoor: One more infra question - do you support VPC logs being exported to our logging account for centralization?
[06:38] Maya Singh: Yes, logs and audit trails can be forwarded to your cloud logging or splunk; we'll include log forwarding steps.
[06:45] Marcus Hale: On billing - if we add region capacity, will billing be consolidated monthly or show per-region line items?
[06:52] Jason Park: Billing is consolidated but line-itemed per region and pool so you can allocate costs. We'll include sample invoice mockup.
[07:01] Lena Ortiz: For our QA team to validate quant, how long to spin up a test cluster in eu-west?
[07:07] Maya Singh: Provisioning Dedicated in a new region typically takes 3-5 business days after contract sign and network setup; for Private on-prem it would be longer. For a short-term eval we can provision a demo cluster quicker - 24-48 hours in some cases - but that depends on capacity.
[07:21] Marcus Hale: Any blockers we should be aware of for July sign?
[07:25] Jason Park: Only security paperwork (NDA/ISA) and region capacity confirmation. If we get those in the next week we can hit your timeline.
[07:33] Lena Ortiz: Ok we'll get Marcus and legal to look at the NDA and confirm region list.
[07:38] Priya Kapoor: Also want the network runbook so our infra team can preconfigure TGW peering.
[07:44] Maya Singh: We'll share the runbook and a checklist for peering and SAML.
[07:49] (short pause)
[07:51] Marcus Hale: On competitors - we've seen benchmarking from Anthropic and Bedrock; how does Redwood stack on latency for our model sizes?
[07:59] Maya Singh: For your family of models, Redwood's tuned runtime often meets or beats alternatives on p95 due to kernel selection and kv-prefix caching. We'll include side-by-side numbers but keep in mind results vary by sequence length and model architecture.
[08:12] Jason Park: Also to note, our cost model tends to be more predictable for committed capacity which helps finance forecasting.
[08:20] Lena Ortiz: Sounds good. Let's talk specifics on tiers - what would a proposed commit look like?
[08:25] Jason Park: I'll propose three tiers in the draft: (A) small bump - +4 reserved GPUs, monthly commit; (B) medium - +8 reserved GPUs + 8 burstable, 12-month commit with 10% discount; (C) large - +12 reserved + autoscale burst with 15% discount plus 6-month review. Each will show expected p95 improvements and cost delta.
[08:46] Marcus Hale: That structure works. We'll likely aim for B and include eu-west dedicated pool.
[08:52] Priya Kapoor: For region-specific compliance, are logs stored in-region only?
[08:58] Maya Singh: We can configure log retention to keep copies in-region and also forward to your central logs depending on your data residency needs. We'll detail retention windows.
[09:08] (several quick confirmations)
[09:12] Jason Park: Ok let's recap next steps - Maya will send benchmark sheet and runbook by Friday (2026-07-23), I'll send draft renewal tiers and sample invoice by Monday (2026-07-26), Marcus to confirm regions by 2026-07-28, and we'll schedule a follow-up to review the draft.
[09:31] Marcus Hale: Works for me. One more: can you run a quick QA diff on 100 samples with and without quant and share results?
[09:38] Maya Singh: Yes we can. We'll do a 100-sample diff and include regression metrics; deliverable with the bench.
[09:45] Lena Ortiz: Great, thanks. Anything else?
[09:49] Priya Kapoor: No, that's it from infra.
[09:52] Jason Park: Thanks everyone. We'll get those artifacts out. We'll follow up in email with the NDA link and attachments.
[09:59] Marcus Hale: Thanks Jason, Maya.
[10:02] Lena Ortiz: Thanks.
[10:04] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: Some product names slightly mis-transcribed (Redwood Dedicated occasionally noted as Redwood Dedicate) and technical terms like KV cache spelled as KV cash in places. Natural speech patterns included.

References/shared artifacts mentioned:
- Renewal tiers draft (to be sent by Jason)
- Benchmark spreadsheet (to be sent by Maya)
- Network runbook (to be sent by Maya)
- SOC2 report (available under NDA)

Recap (final):
- Redwood to produce renewal proposal with three tiers + sample invoice (Jason)
- Redwood SE to share benchmark and runbook and run 100-sample quant diff (Maya)
- Millbrook to confirm regions and review NDA/legal (Marcus/Lena)
- Target sign: August mid-month pending legal and region confirmations

End of transcript.
